html:
The 1984 Winter Olympics were held in Sarajevo from 8 to 19 February 1984, the first Winter Games in a communist country and the only ones in Yugoslavia.

Sarajevo built ski runs on the mountains of Bjelašnica and Jahorina, a bobsleigh track on Trebević and new hotels. The games were seen as well run and friendly, and the British ice dancers Torvill and Dean scored perfect marks. The wolf mascot Vučko became a beloved symbol of the city. Eight years later many Olympic sites were front lines in the siege of Sarajevo; the bobsleigh track was used as an artillery position and the Zetra hall was hit. The games are remembered in Bosnia as the city's last golden moment.
sum: The 1984 Winter Olympics were held in Sarajevo from 8 to 19 February 1984, the first Winter Games in a communist country and the only ones in Yugoslavia.
